column4: Visit note | 2025-07-30 10:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Sharmin Bepari, 48, female. Mrs. Bepari returns for review, reporting persistent complaints of a racing heart and shaky hands that interfere with her daily life. She works as an office cleaner, and she first noticed her symptoms when her clothes became loose during a stay in Mymensingh. She mentions that her heartbeat feels unusually fast even when she is sitting quietly, and she feels jittery throughout the day. She denies any chest pain, shortness of breath at rest, heat intolerance, or visual changes, though she admits to feeling more fatigued than usual. On examination: pulse 119 bpm, BP 127/76 mmHg, weight 85 kg. Thyroid palpation reveals a diffuse, non-tender enlargement without palpable nodules. Her reflexes are brisk, and her hands show a fine tremor. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee, and to rest when her heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-07-30 10:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Uttam Bhattacharya, 68, male. Mr. Bhattacharya presents for his first visit complaining of nausea accompanying a spinning sensation, brief spinning episodes when turning in bed, and dizziness when looking up. He works as a madrasa teacher, and these symptoms began after he bumped his head on a rickshaw hood in Gulshan. He reports no hearing loss, tinnitus, headache, or focal neurological deficits. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, BP 121/75 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 50 kg. Cranial nerves are intact, and cerebellar tests are normal. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-07-30 03:00 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Gautam Chakraborty, 31, male. Mr. Chakraborty attends for review, describing a throbbing headache on one side and light hurting his eyes. He works as a fisherman, and his headaches have grown worse since he started dealing with bright screens at a new job in Old Dhaka. He describes seeing flashing zigzag lights before the attacks accompanied by tingling in one hand. He denies any fever, neck stiffness, weakness, or recent head trauma. On examination: about 11 headache days a month, BP 130/74 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 87 kg. Neurological examination is unremarkable. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-07-31 02:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Mehnaz Shikder, 43, female. Mrs. Shikder comes in for her first visit with painful swallowing, a sore throat, and swollen glands in the neck. She works as an office cleaner, and her symptoms began after shouting at a cricket match in Old Dhaka. She notes one-sided throat pain with difficulty opening the mouth, along with severe discomfort when trying to swallow food or liquids. She denies any shortness of breath or skin rashes. On examination: temperature 102.4°F, BP 118/76 mmHg, pulse 110 bpm, weight 60 kg. Throat examination shows erythematous, enlarged tonsils with patchy exudates and tender submandibular lymphadenopathy. Assessment: Acute tonsillitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to gargle with warm salt water, eat soft food, and drink plenty of fluids. Follow-up in 1 week.
